page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff between raw compute power and memory capacity. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core performance and weak multi-core performance in stress-ng tests. However, memory bandwidth remains stable, with read-only large block bandwidth at 78.48 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 40.34 GB/sec, both scoring in the average range. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations also perform at average levels, achieving 11.14 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides a high density of memory relative to its shared CPU resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. It is suited for large-scale caching layers, in-memory databases, static web serving, and lightweight data processing tasks where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck rather than raw compute speed.
